How does the Done n Dusted API work?

Long image

A

Answer

Done n Dusted is a layered Spring Boot REST API. Three nested resources, 15 endpoints, one path through the code, one error format.

  1. Guild owns Quest, and Quest owns LogEntry; a child is only reachable through its parent URL.1
  2. Every request goes controller, then service, then repository, then PostgreSQL.2
  3. Only the server decides XP; a new log entry always starts as PENDING with 0 XP.3
  4. Every failure becomes the same ApiError JSON with a fitting status code.4

Applies toLD1 labcommit 6f927d7dev profile with embedded PostgreSQL 18

The dev profile starts a real PostgreSQL 18 process on port 55432.5 Its data is temporary, so every start begins from the Flyway seed data. Connect DBeaver or HeidiSQL to localhost:55432, database postgres, user postgres, no password.

2

Which endpoints exist?

ResourcePathMethodsSuccess codes
Guild/api/guilds and /api/guilds/{guildId}GET list, GET one, POST, PUT, DELETE200, 201 with Location, 204
Quest/api/guilds/{guildId}/quests and /{questId}GET list, GET one, POST, PUT, DELETE200, 201 with Location, 204
LogEntry/api/guilds/{guildId}/quests/{questId}/logs and /{logId}GET list, GET one, POST, PUT, DELETE200, 201 with Location, 204

Lists return content, page metadata and self, first, prev, next and last links. Filters and sort survive in every link.

3

What happens when the DM approves an entry?

Diagram structure
  • Client client
  • Error handler handler
  • Controller controller
  • LogEntryService service
  • Repository repo
  • QuestService quests
  • LogEntry entry
  • PostgreSQL db
  • client → controller · PUT /api/guilds/2/quests/6/logs/9
  • controller → handler · alt: bind / validation fails
  • handler → client · alt: 400 ApiError
  • controller → service · update(2, 6, 9, request)
  • service → repo · findByIdAndQuestIdAndQuestGuildId(9, 6, 2)
  • repo → db · SELECT log_entry JOIN quest
  • db → repo · log 9 row (PENDING)
  • repo → service · Optional<LogEntry>
  • service → handler · alt: throws ResourceNotFoundException
  • handler → client · alt: 404 ApiError
  • service → quests · get(2, 6)
  • quests → db · SELECT quest WHERE id=6 AND guild_id=2
  • db → quests · quest row
  • quests → service · Quest (difficulty LEGENDARY)
  • service → handler · alt: throws BusinessRuleException
  • handler → client · alt: 422 ApiError
  • service → entry · approve(80, 0, null, Instant.now())
  • entry → service · status APPROVED, XP frozen, reviewedAt set
  • service → db · UPDATE log_entry (flush on commit)
  • db → service · commit OK
  • service → controller · LogEntry (detached)
  • controller → client · 200 OK application/json LogEntryResponse

Without xpAwarded, the server takes XP from the quest difficulty: LEGENDARY is 8 × 10 = 80 XP.6 PUT is a full replacement, so fields left out of the body become null.

4

How does a log entry change status?

Diagram structure
  • PENDING pending
  • APPROVED approved
  • REJECTED rejected
  • Deleted deleted
  • pending → approved · PUT APPROVED
  • approved → approved · re-approve
  • approved → pending · PUT PENDING
  • pending → rejected · PUT REJECTED
  • approved → rejected · PUT REJECTED
  • rejected → approved · PUT APPROVED
  • rejected → pending · PUT PENDING
  • pending → deleted · DELETE
  • approved → deleted · DELETE
  • rejected → deleted · DELETE

The entity has no status setter. Status and XP change together through approve, reject and resetToPending.8 The database repeats the rule with CHECK constraints, so a PENDING row can never hold XP.9

5

Which check produces which status code?

Diagram structure
  • 404 · 405 e404path
  • 415 Unsupported e415
  • 406 Not Acceptable e406
  • 400 Bad Request e400type
  • 400 Bad Request e400read
  • POST / PUT request req
  • URL + method match? route
  • Content-Type JSON? ctype
  • Accept allows JSON? accept
  • Path IDs are numbers? pathvar
  • Body readable JSON? body
  • @Valid passes? valid
  • Parent chain exists? chain
  • Domain rules hold? rules
  • Name / title free? unique
  • DB constraints pass? commit
  • Success ok
  • 400 + details[] e400valid
  • 404 Not Found e404
  • 422 Unprocessable e422
  • 409 Conflict e409
  • 409 Conflict e409db
  • req → route
  • unique → commit
  • commit → ok
  • route → ctype
  • ctype → accept
  • accept → pathvar
  • pathvar → body
  • body → valid · bound DTO
  • valid → chain
  • chain → rules
  • rules → unique
  • route → e404path
  • commit → e409db
  • ctype → e415
  • accept → e406
  • pathvar → e400type
  • body → e400read
  • valid → e400valid
  • chain → e404
  • rules → e422
  • unique → e409
CodeMeaning in this API
400The request itself is wrong: bad JSON, unknown field, wrong type, failed field validation.
404The resource is missing, or it belongs to a different parent.
409The request is fine but clashes with existing data, such as a taken name.
422The JSON is valid but breaks a domain rule, such as GRIND without targetCount.
